results: Not executed. The gap's next_check names the isolation method: `unshare --pid --fork --mount-proc` with its own port. In a private PID namespace with its own /proc, restore/reindex's same-name process guard sees only processes inside the namespace, so it neither inspects nor depends on the host's ai-memory.service. The previous blocker ('the guard enumerates live host processes, which the isolation rules forbid') therefore does not hold. The same fix round ran `unshare -rn` successfully (transcript calls [8], [12], [27]), so `unshare -rn --pid --fork --mount-proc` with a disposable data dir was available but not tried. Corroboration: the peer receipt evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260923/pins-mem/ai-memory.json on origin/main (5dcf451) records restore refusing with 'refusing to restore: 1 other ai-memory process(es) running (pids: [365])' when run without a PID namespace, which is the failure a private PID namespace removes. Outcome: not_settled (weak deferral).
limits: No restore or reindex was executed; evidence is the quoted source text only.

Remaining: in `unshare -rn --pid --fork --mount-proc`, init a disposable data dir, serve it on its own loopback port with AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL exported, write pages, back up, restore into a fresh dir and reindex, then compare page/session/observation counts and search results with the pre-backup copy.
